name: create_new_element
reason: copyC inlines it as 'drop the attrib when the heap list is empty', but is_empty_dict (:213-216, used at :344) also needs PyDict_CheckExact, so an empty frozendict or empty dict subclass is shared by the copy (EtreeCopy.lean scopes this out without a refutation), and no theorem distinguishes the emptiness branch: CopyShallow and both refutations hold whether or not an empty attrib is dropped.

name: element_add_subelement
reason: addAllC mirrors Element_Check/raise_type_error then the append, and WritersTwins' extend clause pins it against the twin for every list or tuple, non-Elements included (same children, TypeError class), so a version without the check fails it.

name: element_get_attrib
reason: Dicts are values, not objects: getAttribC returns a fresh .dict [] and setC builds its own slot instead of writing through the returned dict, so a get_attrib that creates the dict without storing it in self->extra->attrib (or returns a new one each call) satisfies AttribDict, AttribInvariant and NoBadCall alike.

name: _elementtree_Element_append_impl
reason: appendC is Clinic's subclass_of check then element_add_subelement's append, and WritersTwins pins it against list.append for every Element (non-Elements are refused by Clinic before this body).

name: _elementtree_Element___copy___impl
reason: copyC now copies text, tail and children by reference, but it inherits create_new_element's misdescribed emptiness test: for an empty frozendict or empty dict subclass attrib the C copy shares the object while copyC gives the copy no attrib, a case the scope note excludes and no refutation records.

name: element_setstate_from_attributes
reason: setstateC tracks only the attrib slot: the tag/text/tail stores and their JOIN_SET flags, the children copy loop with its partial state on a bad child (length = i at :1112, the old children dropped), and the restore on resize failure are not modelled, so only the attrib invariant (refuted) touches this body.

name: element_setstate_from_Python
reason: The keyword parse (unknown key -> TypeError) and the hand-off of tag and attrib to element_setstate_from_attributes are mirrored on the path setstateKeepsAttrib_refuted runs ({'tag', 'attrib': ()} stores a tuple), a real invariant violation with bug textlibs-etree-setstate-attrib-systemerror.

name: _elementtree_Element___setstate___impl
reason: SetstateEntry is rfl on setstateEntryC's two-way match, and the PyDict_CheckExact test (:1179) is baked into StateArg (a dict subclass is .other by construction), so a __setstate__ that accepted any dict cannot even be stated; the theorem restates the definition rather than pinning the check.

name: checkpath
reason: Only the str branch is modelled; the bytes branch (:1224-1241) and 'unknown type -> 1' (:1243) are missing, PlainTagTwins holds for checkpath = fun _ => true or fun _ => false alike, and fastPathSound_refuted only fixes its value on one string.

name: _elementtree_Element_extend_impl
reason: extendC is PySequence_Fast (which runs all of an iterator's effects before any append, so one eff covers them) then element_add_subelement per item; WritersTwins pins lists and tuples, non-Elements included, and extendTwins_refuted records the iterator case with bug textlibs-etree-py-twin-setitem.

name: _elementtree_Element_find_impl
reason: The fast-path scan compares str tags with ==, but tags are arbitrary objects and PyObject_RichCompareBool(tag, path) can raise (the rc < 0 return at :1318) or run __eq__ that mutates the children the loop rereads each pass; none of this is expressible in the model.

name: _elementtree_Element_findtext_impl
reason: Same gap as find: the rich comparison of arbitrary tags cannot raise or re-enter in the model (rc < 0 at :1368, children mutated mid-scan).

name: _elementtree_Element_findall_impl
reason: Same gap as find: the rc < 0 failure (:1411) and mutation by __eq__ during the scan are not modelled, since tags are str compared with ==.

name: _elementtree_Element_get_impl
reason: Keys are str, so PyDict_GetItemWithError failing on a key whose __hash__ or __eq__ raises (:1459-1462) is missing, and so is the consequence that with no attrib C returns the default without hashing the key (e.get([]) gives None where the twin's dict.get raises TypeError).

name: element_getitem
reason: getItemC's bounds check after the single negative wrap is :1524-1529 exactly (NULL extra as length 0), and ItemTwins pins value and IndexError class against list indexing for every int index.

name: _elementtree_Element_insert_impl
reason: insertC has Clinic's index conversion, the clamp of :1573-1579, the grow and the shift loop of :1584-1585, and WritersTwins proves it equal to list.insert for every Element and every int index (overflow included).

name: _elementtree_Element_items_impl
reason: itemsC is the NULL check then PyDict_Items (SystemError on a non-dict slot), and AttribDict pins it: after set(k, v) items() is dictSet of the old items in insertion order, and it lists what the getter returns.

name: _elementtree_Element_keys_impl
reason: There is no model of keys(): itemsC stands in for both keys() and items(), so what keys() returns (the keys, as opposed to the pairs) is stated nowhere and a keys() returning items or values would satisfy every theorem.

name: _elementtree_Element_remove_impl
reason: removeLoopC/removeC follow :1680-1718 (identity, then a fallible, re-entrant __eq__ that may change the children, the length re-read each pass, the post-loop extra/length guard with a NULL extra as the empty list), RemoveTwins proves it equal to list.remove for every comparator, and the non-Element case is refuted (removeTwinsAll_refuted, bug textlibs-etree-py-twin-setitem).

name: _elementtree_Element_set_impl
reason: Keys are str, so PyDict_SetItem failing or re-entering through a key's __hash__/__eq__ (:1769) is not expressible; note that set works on the borrowed reference from element_get_attrib (:1765) while get takes a strong one (:1458), so an __eq__ that replaces e.attrib during the insert is exactly the path the model cannot reach.

name: element_setitem
reason: setItemC is bounds first, then Element_Check and store, or the delete shift (:1782-1805); ItemTwins pins it for Elements and deletion, and the non-Element case it excludes is on record as refuted (itemStoreTwins_refuted, bug textlibs-etree-py-twin-setitem).

name: element_subscr
reason: Indexes and slice bounds are Int, so __index__ that raises or mutates the element inside PyNumber_AsSsize_t / PySlice_Unpack (:1816, :1833), the ordering the gh-143200 note at :1826-1828 exists for, is not expressible, and the 'element indices must be integers' branch (:1859-1863, badKeyC) is in no theorem.

name: element_ass_subscr
reason: Slice bounds are Int (no __index__ re-entrancy before the length is read, the gh-143200 note at :1882-1884), the non-index TypeError (:2048-2052) is in no theorem, and SetSliceTwinsSeq assumes every item is an Element although C runs the extended-slice size check (:1979) before the type check (:1999) while the twin type-checks first, so e[::2] = [5] gives ValueError in C and TypeError in the twin, a difference not on record.

name: element_attrib_getter
reason: AttribDict's getter clauses (idempotence, items of the result) hold for a getter that returns a fresh empty dict without storing it, because dicts are compared as values and getAttribC's created dict is never written through; that the getter returns the stored object is not expressible.

name: element_attrib_setter
reason: The deletion branch (_VALIDATE_ATTR_VALUE, AttributeError "can't delete element attribute", :2129) is absent from setAttribC, and AttribDict's setter clause is conditional on success, so a setter that refuses every dict and frozendict satisfies it and AttribInvariant alike.
